abstract: Early embryonic gastrulation requires precise cell fate decisions. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification regulates transcriptome dynamics during cell fate transitions but its upstream transcriptional regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify THAP1 as a direct transcriptional regulator of METTL3, the core m6A methyltransferase. THAP1 loss reduces METTL3 expression and global m6A levels, impairing the activation of genes involved in cell fate transition-associated signaling pathways in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) and rat embryos. Ectopic METTL3 expression in THAP1-knockout mESCs largely rescues transcriptional dysregulation and partially restores m6A modification, RNA stability, and translation. Single-cell RNA sequencing of rat embryos further reveals reduced METTL3 expression and impaired signaling associated with cell fate transitions upon THAP1 loss. Together, these findings establish a conserved THAP1-METTL3 regulatory axis that supports gene expression programs associated with early embryonic cell fate transitions and suggest that its disruption contributes, at least in part, to embryonic lethality following THAP1 deletion.
